questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: It had to be an academically high ranking univeristy while still be easy to get around in the city without a car.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
It has been such a wonderful experience - the only reason why I do not give it 10 is because of the living situation. 
However, the university is bustling with life and such interesting people with all sorts of backgrounds.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: There was SO much information prior to and upon arrival. You get countless emails with a lot of redundant information. It takes a long time to find out what is actually necessary information for you to be updated on.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: At American universities, they expect you to be coming straight out of your parents' house, so they pretty much give you all the assistance you need. Like ALL you need - at some point they went over what you should have in an emergency kit at home (like napkins and stuff)...

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: I had all the help I needed and more if I would have liked.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: They have regular dorms, both single and double rooms (i.e. with a roommate) in suites. You are guaranteed housing on campus.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: They had meal plans with meals served in dining halls. One meal cost around $16. I usually cooked as there was a fully equipped kitchen in my suite.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It is a lot of fun being a constant part of campus. However, it gets tiring to live on such a small place. You basically only have a chair, a desk and a bed - anything else is found on campus itself.

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Everything was satisfactory but tiring to live with at length.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: They have a seperate website just for course description and registration. They even have a timetable feature where you can plan your classes before registering/waitlisting for them.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Exchange students are the last students to register for class. There are only a certain number of students that are entered into each class. However, in the US, they have a "shopping-period" - i.e. you have registered for a lot of classes and then drop the classes you don't like before the period is over. Thereby, if you waitlist for classes, spots are highly likely to open up even after the semester has begun. Additionally, the professors are very approachable and may let you in if you talk to them.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There was an academic advisor available, but she was rather slow at responding.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was waitlisted for a lot of my classes in the beginning, but managed to get into all of them by the end of the registration period.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Book a meeting with the academic advisor to make sure you are aware of all the deadlines in regards to registration - there are a lot more than at KU.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The professors are good!!

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
They were very easy!
In the US, people only do a few courses within their major and the rest covers other academic interests. Therefore, the average American student does not have a very thorough knowledge of their major at undergraduate level. All the economics courses I took turned out to be equivalent to a level 1-4th semester at KU. It even allowed me to do a total of 45 ECTS points - I would never have done that at KU!

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It is a lot more interactive and taught in smaller classes. Participation goes towards your grade. It feels like being back in high school.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
The Global Economy
Economic History of Global Capitalism (approved as "Økonomisk Historie")
Money & Banking
China's Foreign Relations
Advanced Poetry Writing
Research Credit

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I really enjoyed pursuing my hobby at a professional level, which is why I took the course "Advanced Poetry Writing". Do take advantage of this - I am unfortunately not able to transfer these specific ECTS point back to KU because it is outside of my major, but the creative classes do not take up that much time. They have all sorts of creative classes: everything from pottery making to tap dancing and everything in between.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: You pay for a mandatory health insurance when you are an exchange student. That's why the insurance costs I have listed are so high.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Groceries are a lot more expensive in NYC than in Denmark.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There are so many opportunities! They have a club for everything and they are very welcoming even if you are only attending for one semester.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Literally anything you can think of.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I joined a bible study through RUF. I enjoyed the academic approach to studying the bible. The people I met there were also some of the most sweet and welcoming people I have met throughout my stay.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go on the Staten Ferry Island - it is free and gives a beautiful view of the city from the river.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I have lived abroad before, so I found it relatively easy. The American culture is also very welcoming, so it is easy to find friends.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Take advantage of how everybody has a meal plan, so it is easy to meet for meals.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: In the beginning, I had a hard time adjusting to how the city could feel a bit unsafe at times. However, you learn that it is not unsafe; it is just the city that can look a bit odd at times.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The diversity of the student body - everybody has a different background than you, so you hear a lot of interesting stories!

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: If you are even considering it, GO! That's my only important thing:)

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Academically, it has been super interesting to be exposed to economic examples that aren't Danish. Here, North and South America are in focus when examples are made. It has worked as a great source of inspiration for my studies.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Finding out where to get affordable groceries.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
